name: Kindercloak
body:
A mass of darkness sweeps out of sight. A pie goes missing from a windowsill. The murder weapon at a crime scene is replaced with a pile of white stones. The kindercloaks are inscrutable. Are they magical fey? Are they constructs, working toward some bizarre purpose? In fact, they are much more and much less than either, and a bit of everything: They are primitive homunculi from a forgotten time, magically woven from vermin and cornstalks around wood and straw. They are a hivemind, an enormous, world-spanning population dedicated to a single obscure objective.

Physical Description: Kindercloaks resemble humanoid figures in dark cloaks, though the color of cloak can vary; indeed, color is the key mode of differentiation for those who deal often with members of the species. They stand roughly three feet tall and are two feet wide—their cloaks spill down around them in a way that implies rather plump, chinchilla-like forms. Their faces are obscured beneath the cloak, but the eyes glow when the kindercloak is stressed or wants to make a point. When a kindercloak is “naked,” all that can be seen is a blurry mass of shadow—the consequence of their animating magic being rather primitive and centuries-worn. Kindercloaks all weigh exactly thirty pounds, or a hundred and fifty pounds when petrified by light.

Society: The hivemind of kindercloaks is tightly-organized but loosely-bound, and kindercloaks almost never run into one another. The hivemind deliberately assigns only one kindercloak to a given area save in matters of extreme importance to the hive’s mysterious objectives. They are all telepathically and empathically linked. Kindercloaks all possess, in fact, two minds: The dominant personality of the hivemind, which tends to dictate the kindercloak’s actions, and the “recessive” personality of the individual kindercloak in question, which is formed over years of experiences felt only slightly more vividly than the rest of the hive. If a kindercloak is stabbed, all feel some pain, but only that one feels the full extent—otherwise, the hivemind would become debilitative. This lesser personality mainly surfaces in social interactions, and is extremely subtle to non-kindercloaks. Nonetheless, each kindercloak has a little bit of individuality, and there is no easier way to lose a kindercloak as a friend than to forget that.

Relations: Kindercloaks largely avoid contact with other races, and the shorter-lived species, such as halflings, humans, and half-orcs, tend to regard them as enigmas if they know of them at all. Kindercloaks get along best with dwarves and gnomes—dwarves treat kindercloaks with a wary hospitality, and gnomes sometimes form very strong bonds with the strange creatures. Kindercloaks treat elves extremely coolly, and the feeling is mutual: Elves mistrust any creature that so very deliberately avoids the sun.

Alignment and Religion: The overall hivemind of the kindercloaks is relatively well-intentioned, but extremely self-interested, and is best described as True Neutral. Kindercloaks’ secondary alignments, on the other hand, vary. Their alignments are usually close to the hivemind’s, but sometimes arc off due to exceptional events or trauma. This conflict can become a challenge to reconcile, and a kindercloak that is not of neutral alignment can behave especially erratically, sometimes even trying to resist the will of the hive. The hivemind has no religion, but secondary personalities do occasionally favor more mild-mannered gods of dreams and darkness.

Adventurers: Kindercloaks obey the will of the hive, and often the hive tells them to explore the world and learn more to expand its intellect. Kindercloaks with rebellious personalities embrace adventuring as a way to gain more vivid experiences that strengthen their individual personalities further. Sometimes, a kindercloak is sent on a very specific mission on behalf of the hivemind.

Names: Kindercloaks are sexless and the hivemind is genderless, though some individual personalities identify with a specific gender. In the same vein, kindercloaks do not start their lives with names, but rather acquire names over time. Kindercloak names are usually assigned by humanoids, or based on objects the kindercloak sees when it is trying to think of a name.

Names: Blinker, Blue, Cloak, Creepy, Glimmer, Mug, Purple, Rosebush, Stick, Yellow

Core Traits (16 RP)
Ability Score Modifiers: Kindercloaks are swift, and can call upon the knowledge of the hivemind, but they are small and extremely frail. They gain +2 Dexterity, +2 Intelligence, –2 Strength, and –4 Constitution: –2 RP
Type: Kindercloaks have the half-construct subtype, and cannot be raised or resurrected. They still need to breathe, eat and sleep. They gain a +2 racial bonus on saving throws against disease, mind-affecting effects, poison, and effects that cause either exhaustion or fatigue. 7 RP
Size: Kindercloaks are Small creatures and gain a +1 size bonus to their AC, a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a –1 penalty on combat maneuver checks and to their CMD, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks.
Speed: Kindercloaks are fast for their size, and have a base speed of 30 feet. 1 RP
Languages: Kindercloaks begin play speaking Common and can communicate via telepathy with all other kindercloaks on the same plane. Kindercloaks with high Intelligence scores can learn any languages they want (except secret languages, such as Druidic). 1 RP
Linked Mind: Kindercloaks gain a +2 racial bonus on all Will saves. Should they fail a Will save while within 100 feet of another kindercloak, that kindercloak must immediately save as well or be affected by the same effect. 1 RP
Vermin Empathy: This ability functions as a druid’s wild empathy, using the kindercloak’s HD as its druid level, except that a kindercloak can only use it on vermin. A kindercloak gains a +2 racial bonus on this check. 2 RP
Writhing Form: Kindercloaks gain a +2 racial bonus on Stealth checks and Escape Artist checks, and these skills are always class skills for them. This improves to a +8 bonus on Escape Artist checks to squeeze into small spaces. 5 RP
Uncloak: As a full-round action, a kindercloak may choose to remove its cloak, exiting in the form of a foggy, amorphous entity. This is a vulnerable, in-between state for the kindercloak. However, in this state, the kindercloak always gains at least partial concealment when in areas of darkness, even against creatures with low-light vision or darkvision. The kindercloak is still solid, and it retains its equipment. It can return to its cloaked state by putting the cloak back on (or putting on a new, similarly concealing article of clothing) as a full-round action. When uncloaked in an area of bright light, a kindercloak is petrified (as flesh to stone), and remains so until the cloak is restored or the light level drops below bright levels. While petrified, the kindercloak appears to be a small column of frozen smoke. 1 RP
Darkvision: Kindercloaks see perfectly in the dark up to 60 feet. 2 RP
Base Components: When brought to negative hit points equal to or greater than their Constitution score, the kindercloak’s enchantments fade and it dissolves into the components originally used to create it: a toad, a spider, a rat, and several old cornstalks. The animals immediately scatter, behaving like normal beasts. All components must be brought together into a place of darkness and have bestow curse, limited wish, wish or miracle cast upon them to restore the kindercloak to animation at a single hit point. If one or two components are dead or destroyed, but are still brought to the cloak, the restored kindercloak takes an equal number of permanent negative levels. If more than two are destroyed, the kindercloak cannot be restored. The original cornstalks can be replaced—the animals cannot. –2 RP
Alternate Racial Traits

While kindercloaks have very little variation in their physical forms—the magic that put them all together is, definitively, quite uniform—some have managed to distinguish themselves in the years since their creation. The following racial traits may be selected instead of existing kindercloak traits.

Children of Darkness: Some kindercloaks are particularly suited to the shadows bound within them. These kindercloaks can see perfectly in darkness of any kind out to 60 feet, including that created by spells such as deeper darkness. This racial trait replaces vermin empathy and darkvision.
Compression: Due to the great age of their magic, the form of a kindercloak is fairly primitive and ill-defined, like an unfinished blob of clay. Some kindercloaks have learned to exploit this strangeness, weakening their magic further to stretch and bend the rules of their own physicality. These kindercloaks can move through areas as small as one-quarter their space without squeezing or one-eighth their space when squeezing. Kindercloaks with this trait can only uncloak safely in dim or darker areas—if uncloaked in areas of normal light or brighter, they are petrified. This racial trait alters uncloak.
